title: The impact of cleft lip and palate (CLP) on the oral microbiome, the local immune response and clinical parameters during interdisciplinary orthodontic treatments
summary:
In newborns with cleft lip and palate (CLP), orthodontic treatment with palatal plates is necessary shortly after birth to ensure feeding and to promote the growth of the alveolar segments. Orthodontic treatment with removable or fixed appliances is often necessary for children and adolescents with CLP in order to promote the growth of the upper jaw and to align misaligned or
misaligned or severely rotated teeth. Patients with CLP have poorer oral health, i.e. an increase in dental plaque, caries, gum disease, tooth loosening, bone loss and, in the worst case, tooth loss. Recent studies have found an "imbalance" between "good" (protective) and "bad" (pathogenic) bacteria in the oral microbiome (= all microorganisms in the mouth), i.e. dysbiosis, in newborns with CLP. Dysbiosis and increased inflammation levels in the mouth could impact the bone metabolism of patients with LKGS and thus alter the success of treatment. The aim of the study is to investigate the oral microbiome, local inflammation, maxillary growth in infants and tooth movement during orthodontic treatment in patients with CLP at different ages. The aim is to develop new preventive, interdisciplinary treatment concepts between orthodontics, oral and maxillofacial surgery, gynecology and pediatrics.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Newborns with cleft lip and palate and their mothers
- Newborns without cleft lip and palate malformation and their mothers
- Children and adolescents with cleft lip and palate 
- Children and adolescents without cleft lip and palate malformation
Exclusion criteria:
Withdrawal of the declaration of consent by the parents/legal guardians
